That suggests no enlargement of the heart, so probably not something like hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Putting this together: The blood pressure is high in the right arm. The pulses are weaker in the femoral area, which might indicate a narrowing somewhere in the aorta, like coarctation. The systolic murmur and ejection click could point towards aortic stenosis or a bicuspid aortic valve. A bicuspid valve can sometimes cause a click and a murmur, especially if there's some stenosis. The fact that the femoral pulses are trace suggests that blood flow to the lower extremities is reduced, which would happen if there's a coarctation because it's a narrowing of the aorta. So, coarctation of the aorta is a possibility. Another thought is aortic stenosis, which can also cause a murmur and high blood pressure, especially if it's severe. But coarctation is more likely associated with decreased pulses in the lower extremities. Also, the point of maximal impulse is normal, so no enlargement of the ventricles, which would be the case in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or other conditions causing a heart murmur.
